entries.caption: Lace the cables to the hose
entries.spoken: Loose cables on a LowRider flap, snag and chafe, and can yank a plug mid-cut.

more.spoken: The fix? Cable lacing: the method NASA specifies for its mission hardware.

sources.source: NASA-STD-8739.4A, Workmanship Standard for Crimping, Interconnecting Cables, Harnesses, and Wiring, Revision A with Change 4
sources.says: "This standard applies to production and processing of mission hardware"

sources.source: NASA-STD-8739.4A, Workmanship Standard for Crimping, Interconnecting Cables, Harnesses, and Wiring, Revision A with Change 4
sources.says: "Continuous lacing shall be achieved using running lockstitches as shown in Figure 9-5."

sources.source: Wikipedia, Cable lacing, web page
sources.says: "Cable lacing is a method for tying wiring harnesses and cable looms, traditionally used in telecommunication, naval, and aerospace applications."

sources.source: Wikipedia, Cable lacing, web page
sources.says: "Some organizations have in-house standards to which cable lacing must conform, for example NASA specifies its cable lacing techniques in chapter 9 of NASA-STD-8739.4."

more.spoken: Tight, tidy, tough: one tape, no sharp zip-tie tails, and one cut stitch won't unravel the rest.

sources.source: NAVSHIPS 900171, Electronic Installation Practices Manual, Chapter 9 Cabling, Section 7 Lacing and Binding, Change 2
sources.says: "the \"over and under\" form is necessary to prevent unraveling of entire cable lacing, in the event one or more stitches are cut"

more.uncited: "tight, tidy, tough" and "no sharp zip-tie tails" are the tutorial's own

sources.source: NASA-STD-8739.4A, Workmanship Standard for Crimping, Interconnecting Cables, Harnesses, and Wiring, Revision A with Change 4
sources.says: "Harness designs and routing shall provide support and protection to harnesses and cables so that they are protected from abrasion, cold flow, cut through, vibration, chafing, flexing, and sharp edges."

sources.source: NASA-STD-8739.4A, Workmanship Standard for Crimping, Interconnecting Cables, Harnesses, and Wiring, Revision A with Change 4
sources.says: "Provision shall be made for stress relief in wires entering connectors from harnesses"

entries.uncited: "flap" and "snag" are the tutorial's own (the picture shows the loose cables swaying); "yank a plug" is the tutorial's reading of NASA §7.2.28's stress relief at connectors; which cables ride with the core is shown, not said (d19: the problem in one line, the reveal sooner)

entries.caption: One bundle, moving together
entries.spoken: Now watch the core travel: the hose, cord and sleeve flex together, held by every stitch along the run.

more.spoken: One last tip: lace with the hose already in its working bend, and keep the tape flat, never twisted.

sources.source: NAVSHIPS 900171, Electronic Installation Practices Manual, Chapter 9 Cabling, Section 7 Lacing and Binding, Change 2
sources.says: "When bends occur in cable runs, always make the bend before lacing, to keep the bend in place (Figure 9-65)."

sources.source: WireCare, Tying a marline hitch with lacing tape, web page
sources.says: "Keeping the lacing tape as flat and free of twists as possible"

sources.source: NAVSHIPS 900171, Electronic Installation Practices Manual, Chapter 9 Cabling, Section 7 Lacing and Binding, Change 2
sources.says: "When the conductors are properly laced, they support each other and make a single, neat cable."
